name: spriggans

attributes.attribute: ghosts of giants that now act as fairies

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Spriggans are Cornish folk figures. They are the ghosts of a race of giants, reduced to fairies. They guard other fairies as bodyguards. They are playful but not violent. A spriggan will chase an intruder from a fairy gathering rather than hurt him. They are old thieves. They steal butter and other valuables from the fields. Some stories set them in old mounds and ruins, watching a buried treasure. Other Cornish tales give a giant the same charge of the land.
